title: M. caprae as a goat-associated MTBC name
dek: A Wikipedia animal-adapted neighbour of M. bovis. Still MTBC. Still not an NTM. Still a speciation problem for NAATs.
story: M. caprae appears on Wikipedia as an animal-adapted MTBC member historically tied to goats and other ungulates, and as a cause of zoonotic human TB in regions that keep those animals.
The lab trap is identical to bovis: MTBC-positive NAAT, then a human pulmonary prior that assumes Mtb sensu stricto. Caprae is not a subspecies you can ignore in a barcode.
Do not merge caprae into bovis in a clinical report just because both are 'bovine-ish'. Names exist so surveillance and PZA/intrinsic-resistance logic stay honest.
deep: RD patterns sit with the animal-adapted clade (RD9 lost). Confirm with SNPs, not with a single farm history.
WHO disease treatment is still TB treatment once species and DST are known; the epithet is not a fourth drug.
Wildlife and livestock names on Wikipedia are epidemiologic hints. They do not replace an interview.
tb-mtbc remains the barcode plate; this card is the named leaf.
